ArtifactKind.description:
Type of an artifact (SPEC-0001, Common rules): the value of `kind`, which selects the schema of the document.

- `brief`: A short statement of an idea or a scope of work, input of the council.
- `council_report`: The report of the council on a brief.
- `gate`: The tracker issue on which a person approves a brief or a council report.
- `milestone`: A milestone of the roadmap.
- `epic`: An epic of a milestone.
- `story`: A user story of an epic.
- `specification`: A living specification of one capability.
- `change`: A change delta of a living specification.
- `task`: A task of an epic, closed by one pull request.
- `handover`: The hand-over record of a session.

Check.description: A check of the engine: a stable `snake_case` identifier, written in `diagnostics.checks` and in `diagnostics.not_done`. Each value is a constant of the core, documented with the command that runs it. It serialises as its identifier.

Code.description: A stable error code, a `snake_case` identifier. Codes are never renamed or reused (ADR 0009 C8); every code of the engine is a constant of this type, so that one place lists them all. It serialises as its identifier.

DefaultApplied.description: A default the engine applied on behalf of the caller (ADR 0009 C2): an entry of `meta.defaults_applied`, `{pointer, value, reason, message}`. `message` is optional and left out of the serialised form when not given. The value applied is never null: null means not given (C2).

message.description: Why the default applies, for a person; absent when not given.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer, from the root of the input, to where the default applies. With the reason `current_command_version`, the pointer `""` designates the context of the command, its version, which has no place in the input.

reason.description: Stable `snake_case` identifier of why the default applies, documented with the command that applies it.

DefaultReason.description: Why the engine applied a default: a stable `snake_case` identifier, the field `reason` of an entry of `meta.defaults_applied`. Each value is a constant of the core, documented with the command that applies it; it is not a reason of C3. It serialises as its identifier.

Diagnostics.description: The field `diagnostics`: what the engine reports beside the result. All three lists are always written, `[]` when empty.

checks.description: Identifiers of the checks the engine ran, documented with the command that runs them.

not_done.description: Checks the engine did not run, each with its reason.

warnings.description: Warnings, in the shape of an error; the input is not refused for them.

DocumentSummary.description: What the engine read of one document. A member is absent when the document does not give it, or gives it with another type.

id.description: Identifier of the artifact: as read after its schema for a type whose schema is built, as received for a type without one.

input_kind.description: Input type, from `input_kind` of the entry.

kind.description: Artifact type, from the member `kind` of the document.

origin.description: Where the document was read, as given in the input.

status.description: Status of the artifact: after migration to the current version of its schema for a type whose schema is built, as received for a type without one.

Error.description:
A refusal of the engine, with the fields of ADR 0009 C3, its `source`, and `document`, the index of the document of the input it belongs to (SPEC-0004 R2).

`pointers`, `expected`, `fix`, `source` and `document` are optional and left out of the serialised form when not given; a list given empty is written `[]` (C2).

code.description: Stable `snake_case` code of the error; codes are never renamed or reused (ADR 0009 C8).

document.description: Index, from 0, in the input array `documents` of the document the error belongs to; absent for an error of the input itself (SPEC-0004 R2).

expected.description: The values accepted at `pointer`, never a pattern; `[]` when no value is accepted; absent when not given.

fix.description: The closest member for a misspelt key, or a corrected value; absent when none can be derived.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person; its wording is not part of the contract.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer to the faulty value: into the document given by `document` for an error of a document, into the input sent otherwise; empty for the whole document or the whole input. With the code `command_input` and the reason `enum`, the pointer `""` designates the context of the command, its requested version, which has no place in the input.

pointers.description: Pointers to the other values involved, such as both sides of a conflict; absent when none is given.

reason.description: Why the input was refused (ADR 0009 C3).

source.description: Where the faulty value is stored; absent for a document sent directly.

ErrorReport.description: Every error found in one pass (ADR 0009 C3): the members of the first error, and every error, the first included, in `errors`.

code.description: Stable `snake_case` code of the error; codes are never renamed or reused (ADR 0009 C8).

document.description: Index, from 0, in the input array `documents` of the document the error belongs to; absent for an error of the input itself (SPEC-0004 R2).

errors.description: Every error, in the order found; the first equals the members of the report.

expected.description: The values accepted at `pointer`, never a pattern; `[]` when no value is accepted; absent when not given.

fix.description: The closest member for a misspelt key, or a corrected value; absent when none can be derived.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person; its wording is not part of the contract.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer to the faulty value: into the document given by `document` for an error of a document, into the input sent otherwise; empty for the whole document or the whole input. With the code `command_input` and the reason `enum`, the pointer `""` designates the context of the command, its requested version, which has no place in the input.

pointers.description: Pointers to the other values involved, such as both sides of a conflict; absent when none is given.

reason.description: Why the input was refused (ADR 0009 C3).

source.description: Where the faulty value is stored; absent for a document sent directly.

InputHash.description: The SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the input, in lower-case hexadecimal: `meta.input_hash` (ADR 0009 C1). It serialises as its string.

InputKind.description:
Type of an input (SPEC-0001, Inputs), which has no `kind` member.

- `pull_request`: A pull request: title, body, branch and labels.
- `commit`: A commit message: header and body.
- `handover_input`: A hand-over submitted by an agent, before the engine fills its own fields.

Meta.description: The field `meta`: how the result was produced; nothing in it depends on the machine or the moment.

command_version.description: Version of the input and output schemas of the command, from 1.

defaults_applied.description: Every default the engine applied, in order (ADR 0009 C2); `[]` when none.

dry_run.description: Whether the command only reported the changes it would make.

engine_version.description: Version of the engine that produced the result.

envelope_version.description: Version of the shape of the envelope, from 1.

input_hash.description: SHA-256, in lower-case hexadecimal, of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the input.

NotDone.description: A check the engine did not run, and why: an entry of `diagnostics.not_done`, `{check, reason}`.

check.description: Identifier of the check, documented with the command that runs it.

reason.description: Why the check was not run.

NotDoneReason.description:
Why a check was not run: the field `reason` of an entry of `diagnostics.not_done`. It serialises as its identifier; clients accept values they do not know (C5).

- `not_built`: The part of the engine that runs the check is not built yet.
- `input_absent`: The input the check needs was not given, for example the base revision of a status check.

Origin.description: Where a document was read: exactly one of `file`, `issue`, `milestone`, which the core checks. The member present tells the form, with no tag, as for `source` of an error: a choice without a kind, against the letter of ADR 0009 C4, so that the input and the error report write a place the same way (plan of SPEC-0001).

file.description: Path of the file relative to the root of the project.

issue.description: A tracker issue, by its number.

milestone.description: A tracker milestone, by its number.

Pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON pointer; its root is stated where it is used. Empty for the whole value, or a sequence of `/`-prefixed reference tokens in which `~` is written `~0` and `/` is written `~1`. It serialises as its string.

Reason.description:
Why the engine refused an input, or `internal` when it failed to compute the result: the documented enum of ADR 0009 C3 and its amendment of 2026-11-20. It serialises as its identifier; clients accept values they do not know (C5).

- `syntax`: The input is not well-formed.
- `missing`: A required field is absent.
- `unknown_field`: A field is not part of the schema.
- `duplicate`: A value that must be unique appears more than once.
- `type`: A value has the wrong type.
- `enum`: A value is not one of the accepted values.
- `conflict`: Two values contradict each other.
- `requires`: A field is given without another field it requires.
- `range`: A number is outside its accepted range.
- `length`: A string or a list is too short or too long.
- `state`: The current state or the environment does not allow the command, for example an input that cannot be read.
- `stale`: The expected revision is older than the state (ADR 0009 C6).
- `internal`: The engine could not compute the result: the input may be valid (ADR 0009 C3, amended on 2026-11-20). The command exits with code 5, not 1 (C7).

Source.description: Where the faulty value is stored: `file`, with `line` when the line is known, for a repository file; `issue` for a tracker issue; `milestone` for a tracker milestone. Absent for a document sent directly. Exactly one form is given, never an empty object; the schema checks only that `line` comes with `file`.

file.description: Path of the file relative to the root of the project.

issue.description: Number of the tracker issue, from 1.

line.description: Line of the faulty value in `file`, counted from 1; absent when it is not known, never guessed.

milestone.description: Number of the tracker milestone, from 1.

ValidateData.description: The data of a result of `validate` that accepted the set.

documents.description: One summary per entry of the input `documents`, in the same order; `[]` when the input has none.

description: The result of one command (ADR 0009 C1): its `data` when it succeeded (exit code 0), or the `error` report when its input was refused (exit code 1), the channel was not used as documented (code `usage`, exit code 2), the input could not be read (code `input_unreadable`, exit code 3) or the engine failed to compute it (exit code 5); what the engine reports beside the result; and how the result was produced. A failure is told apart from a refusal by the reason `internal` of its errors. Exactly one of `data` and `error` is given; the schema checks only that `error` is given when `data` is absent.

data.description: The result of the command; absent when the command did not succeed.

diagnostics.description: What the engine reports beside the result.

error.description: Every error found in one pass; absent when the command succeeded.

title: Envelope
